why: The node table is two singly linked lists that may merge into a shared suffix, which is the classic intersection-of-two-lists problem. Either mark all nodes on list A and walk B until a marked node, or use the two-pointer trick that switches heads so both pointers travel lenA + lenB steps.
hints: Intersection means the same node index, not equal values. Once two chains meet, what happens to the rest of their paths?
They share everything after the meeting point. So the first node of B that also lies on A is the answer: record A's nodes, then walk B.

Mark A's nodes in a boolean array (O(n) space), then walk B and return the first marked index; or, for O(1) space, run pointers pa and pb and switch each to the other head when it hits -1; they meet at the intersection or both reach -1.
pitfalls: Either head can be -1 (empty list); then the answer is -1.
If both heads are the same node, that head is the answer.
next can have up to 2 * 10^5 entries; walk iteratively, not recursively.
